column1: # The row patterns of `cells-outcome-sweep.tsv`: each distinct pattern once, with the rows
# that share it and the principle that gives it (P0-P7 and E1-E3 of S5-principles.md, the
# design's S1 (b), L1-L5 and Q1-Q3, and the S5.0 and S5.0g rulings). It is the reviewed
# judgement check 5's `SWEEP` reason names: the sweep's tuples no case covers are judged
# KRS_CELLS_PATTERNS_RECORD=1, which keeps the principle of every pattern whose answers are
# unchanged and leaves a new one's empty: the test fails until it is written.
# A pattern is exact: a table and the answers, cell by cell, of one row group across the
# table's columns (the sweep's short names and `|product:` marks).
# - readable, claim; cells; init: a row group is a side and a stack, and its pattern is its
#   rows, path `-`, `?` and `*` (init: `-` only), one line each. readable and claim have the same
#   columns, so they share patterns; a member names its forms. A row's `other` is a
#   function of its form, side and stack, so a member determines it.
# - children: a row group is one result of the sweep's children section, its pattern the
#   answers in readable, claim and cells! (whose row writes each record as its fragment); a
#   member is its stack, `other` and result, in readable's spelling.
# - children, init: a row group is one value, its pattern the one answer.
# - the `more` tables (readable, claim more; cells more; init more) print each form's
#   further single-entry spellings (the pattern review's gaps G7, G8, G9) as tables of their
#   own, with the same rows, and cells back the computation's back items in cells! (E1 in
#   every form, the fixes review's F-6); children, base matched nowhere is the children
#   table's reading where nothing binds an update's label (S5.0g:P-R3); children, fragment
#   child a group record's Map, List or computation child in a subject and a result (the
#   fixes review's F-1), its member the row's side, stack, `other` and entry.
# Lines: `ID  PATH|answers  ANSWERS..` (the pattern), `ID  member  ..` (each row group that
# has it), `ID  principle  TEXT`. IDs number the patterns in the order their first member is
# The path rule, S5.0g:R3 (each main pattern's `?` and `*` lines): an entry naming a cell
#   below a `?` or `*` ancestor is judged on its own layers first (the form step, then P3
#   against the cell's own stack, refusals inside its marks included) and those refusals
#   stand; whatever they admit is then refused for the ancestor (design:S1b): `owp` below
#   `?`, `cwi` below `*`. A pairing refusal of the `-` row (rm, uor, atc, Q3's overwrite cir,
#   S5.0:F3's open record over an existing group, map-collection-key, record-update-base)
#   comes after the path, so the path class replaces it (S5.0g:P-R12), as it does the
#   product's List collection limitations at the pairing (both ends, a back instance kept
#   in place: `ils`). The product's other departures (design:M3's readable `mrr` at the
#   kind step, design:M3's `cells!` `arm` and E3's `ir` at the form step) come before the
# Citations: every principle line cites the IDs of this registry, and only these (a test
#   fails on a line that cites none, an unknown one, or a ruling by a bare number):
#   P0: an entry means the K configuration it lowers to; a spelling Rust reads otherwise is refused (S5-principles.md §1 P0; scope: every form; any stack)
#   P1: an entry denotes the content of one cell at any depth; the declaration fixes its stack: ?, *, then a computation, a leaf or a group (S5-principles.md §1 P1; scope: every form; any stack)
#   P2: each layer has one mark per form, read lexically; a cons list's brackets end in their rest (S5-principles.md §1 P2; scope: every form; any stack)

#   P3: one judgement in every form, the entry's head against the whole stack: (a), (b), (c); a missing outer layer is named only where the inside passes form and kind (S5-principles.md §1 P3; scope: every form; any stack)
#   P3a: the outermost layer's mark admits the entry, and its inside is judged against the next layer (S5-principles.md §1 P3 (a); scope: every form; any stack)
#   P3b: a mark of a layer the cell has nowhere gives that mark's class (S5-principles.md §1 P3 (b); scope: every form; any stack)
#   P3c: a deeper layer's mark, or a value where the outermost layer has a mark, gives the missing outer layer's class (S5-principles.md §1 P3 (c); scope: every form; any stack)
#   P4: form, then kind (P3), then pairing, then sorts (the lattice), each answered by the first layer that can know it (S5-principles.md §1 P4; scope: every form; any stack)

#   P5: a subject constrains and binds; a result is the new content; None tests absence by creation; an initializer is a complete result, a * cell's value one instance's template (S5-principles.md §1 P5; scope: every form; any stack)

#   P6: at a content root .. is K's ...: a subject matches the rest, a result keeps it with .. or puts a named one back with ..name; records follow Rust, a bare .. in a result being the template of a created instance or of a ? cell created over None (S5-principles.md §1 P6; scope: every form; any stack)
#   P7: readable abbreviates cells!: a readable entry is admitted exactly where the cells! entry it abbreviates is (S5-principles.md §1 P7; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)

#   E1: the computation is read from its front: .. ends it (computation-back-item, a stated exception of every form, S5.0g:F-6) (S5-principles.md §1, the exceptions; scope: every form; stacks with computation)
#   E2: the continuation has no readable value spelling (now Q3) (S5-principles.md §1, the exceptions; scope: readable, claim; stacks with computation)
#   E3: an initializer's k![..] takes no ..pgm (a stated exception) (S5-principles.md §1, the exceptions; scope: init; any stack)
#   Q1: a subject entry that constrains nothing is a lint; a result over an unmatched cell is an overwrite (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4, decisions in force; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)

#   Q2: one collection instance is a value only in an ordered collection; an unordered one's instance is chosen by a written record (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4, decisions in force; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with *)
#   Q3: a readable rule never drops or captures the continuation (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4, decisions in force; scope: readable, claim; any stack)
#   L1: presence is lexical (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4, decisions in force (D3); scope: every form; any stack)
#   L3: initializer brackets on a ? cell with no List layer give bracket-reading (as S5.0g:R7 words it) (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4, decisions in force (D3); scope: init; stacks with ?)
#   L4: a group record at a configuration position names every child or writes .. (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4, decisions in force (D3); scope: every form; stacks with group or *)

#   design:S1b: an entry naming a cell below a ? or * ancestor is refused for the outermost such ancestor (owp, cwi), the rule forms' (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4 §2.3, rows changed in revision 4; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)
#   design:R3: Some(e) admits e by the underlying kind (the design's ruling 3) (S5-principles.md §2 row 55; scope: every form; stacks with ?)
#   design:R4: braces on a Set leaf are instances-on-plain-cell (the design's ruling 4) (S5-principles.md §2 row 56; scope: readable, claim; stacks with leaf Set)

#   design:R6: cells! judges the outermost layer first, withdrawn: one order for every form, a cells! wrapper on a ? or * cell is cell-wrapper (S5-principles.md §3 item 1 (A); scope: cells; stacks with ? or *)

#   design:M3: a map read has no result side until M3: readable { k -> v, .. } in a result is map-read-in-result and a cells! result's k::map![.., ..] at a content root (Cell(..)'s argument, a record field's value) the product's arm, both stated limitations (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4 §2.3, the C-lims; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)

#   design:rev4-R10: an instance child's other side is the labelled subject instance's same child (..me); a created instance's child has none (S5-cell-kinds.md rev. 4, revision 4 table, R10; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with *)
#   S5.0:F1: None over a matched ? cell removes it with its rest, admitted (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0 rulings; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with ?)
#   S5.0:F2: a named rest in a result is alias-outside-pattern (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0 rulings; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)

#   S5.0:F3: with ruling 1: a bare .. on a result group record of a group that exists, matched or overwritten, is open-record-outside-pattern; only a created instance has defaults (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0 rulings; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with group)
#   S5.0:R3: any @ in a result is refused (S5.0's ruling 3) (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0 rulings; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)
#   S5.0:R4: any @ in an initializer is refused (S5.0's ruling 4) (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0 rulings; scope: init; any stack)
#   S5.0g:D-1: a result pairs its rests at every content root, a group or instance record's children included (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g D-1; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with group or *)

#   S5.0g:D-2: a Map collection's instance is keyed by its first child; an update writes the key, if at all, as its subject's key binder (with S5.0g's ruling 2), else map-collection-key (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g D-2 and "ruled next"; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with * Map)
#   S5.0g:D-3: a fragment of the position's group is read as its record, for pairing and Q1's lint (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g D-3; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with group or *)
#   S5.0g:D-4: k::fragment![crate::G { a: x }] is record-missing-children, as its readable form (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g D-4; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with group or *)
#   S5.0g:D-5: a * value is one instance's template at every depth (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g D-5; scope: init; any stack)
#   S5.0g:key: a created Map instance must write its key (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g "ruled next"; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with * Map)

#   S5.0g:R3: the cell's own form, mark and kind refusals come before the path refusal, which replaces only what they admit and pairing (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g part (a) review R3; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)

#   S5.0g:R4: a bare .. on a built record that is not a created instance is open-record-outside-pattern where it leaves a field open; after every field it defaults none (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g R4 and the vacuous-rest ruling; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)
#   S5.0g:R7: L3 holds on a ? cell with no List layer; on a ? List the brackets are its leaf's mark (P3c) (tickets/S5-0g-review-a.md R7; scope: every form; stacks with ?)
#   S5.0g:R9: an update writing a Map key as the same literal its subject matched keeps it (README.md §12 lane 3, S5.0g part (a) review R9; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with * Map)
#   S5.0g:P-R1: a cons list's back lowers to no K: cons-list-back-item, a kind refusal inside the leaf's mark (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes.md ruling 1; scope: every form; stacks with Cons)

#   S5.0g:P-R2: a cells! result's Cell(k::map![.., ..]) is a content root, judged by kind and pairing; arm only where the literal is no content root, a readable map! everywhere (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes.md ruling 2; scope: readable, claim, cells; any stack)

#   S5.0g:P-R3: an update whose label names no subject instance creates an instance where the sentence binds the label elsewhere, and is record-update-base where it binds it nowhere (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes.md ruling 3; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with *)
#   S5.0g:P-R4: brackets on a Set or Map collection are instance-list-shape, whatever they hold (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes.md ruling 4; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with * Set or * Map)
#   S5.0g:P-R5: a missing outer layer is named only where the inside passes form and kind against the deeper layers (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes.md ruling 5; scope: every form; any stack)

#   S5.0g:P-R12: under a path, an ancestor's own pairing decides whether a group is created, so F3's refusal is pairing and the path class replaces it (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes.md ruling 7; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with group)

#   S5.0g:P-R13: a ? cell created over None has a template (the initializer's k::absent!(v)), so its bare .. is admitted (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes.md ruling 7, P6 as amended; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with ?)

#   S5.0g:F-1: a field's direct value in a group record, an instance record or a fragment at a configuration position is its child's entry and content root, as Cell(..)'s argument is: a cells! fragment's k::map![.., ..] child is judged by kind and pairing; deeper, in a term, it stays arm (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes-2.md ruling 1; scope: readable, claim, cells; stacks with group or *)

#   S5.0g:F-6: E1 holds in every form: the computation is read from its front, so cells! KCell(.., x) and KCell(x, .., y) are computation-back-item as readable [.., x] is (tickets/S5-0g-b-review-fixes-2.md ruling 6; scope: every form; stacks with computation)
# reviewed: S5-0g-pattern-review.md (the 86 patterns of 90858e27a); the patterns its rulings moved and the new tables, by S5.0g part (b) item 2 fixes, not yet

column3: Subject on the computation: Some/None pop, braces iop, map notation mna (P3b); [x, ..] and [x] ok (P3a, P5: they constrain and bind); [..] ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint: it matches every content and binds nothing, on a cell the result leaves); [.., x] cbi (E1 in every form, S5.0g:F-6: the computation is read from its front, so `..` ends it; a refusal inside the mark, so it stands under a path); [x, r @ ..] cir (Q3: a readable rule never captures the continuation; a refusal inside the mark, so it stands under a path); x, _, 0 and every record cw (P3c: a value where the computation has its mark; E2 for the whole binder). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a plain Int or Set leaf: Some/None pop, every bracket spelling br (no layer brackets mark, no instance layer), braces iop (on the Set leaf too, design:R4), map notation mna (P3b); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); 0 and the records sort (values: the lattice, P4's sort step, judges a record of another sort). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a List leaf: every bracket spelling ok, [.., x] and [x, r @ ..] included (P3a; P6: a subject `..` matches the unwritten rest and `r @ ..` names it; the builtin List is matched at either end); [..] ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); braces iop, map notation mna, Some/None pop (P3b); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry; 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a cons leaf: as on a List leaf (P2: brackets mark both), but [.., x] cons-list-back-item (S5.0g:P-R1, P0: a cons list is built from its front, so an item after its rest is no constructor pattern and lowers to no K; a refusal inside the leaf's mark, so it stands under a path); [x, ..], [x] and [x, r @ ..] ok (P3a, P6); [..] ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); braces iop, map notation mna, Some/None pop (P3b); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry; 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a Map leaf: { y -> x, .. } ok (P3a: the map read, its rest framed, P6); brackets br (no bracket or instance layer), Some/None pop, braces of records iop (P3b; P2 reads braces of records as instances, lexically, not as map notation); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on the plain group G, which has no mark (P2): Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop, map notation mna (P3b); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); 0 sort (the lattice); G { a: x, .. } and G { a: x, b: y, .. } ok (P6: a subject record's `..` leaves the other children unconstrained); G { a: x } rmc (L4: without `..` a record names every child; a kind refusal, so it stands under a path). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on `? leaf Int`: Some(x) ok (P3a); None atc (P5: K tests absence only by creating the cell, and the result leaves it); brackets br, braces iop, map notation mna (P3b: no layer has these marks); x, _, 0 and every record owp (P3c: a value under `?`, whose inside the Int leaf passes, S5.0g:P-R5). Paths: S5.0g:R3 (a pairing refusal is replaced by the ancestor's class).

Subject on `? leaf List`: Some(x) ok (P3a); None atc (P5); every bracket spelling owp (P3c: the List leaf's mark under `?`, S5.0g:R7, its inside passing against the leaf, S5.0g:P-R5); braces iop, map notation mna (P3b); x, _, 0 and every record owp (P3c). Paths: S5.0g:R3 (a pairing refusal is replaced by the ancestor's class).

Subject on `? leaf Map`: Some(x) ok (P3a); None atc (P5); { y -> x, .. } owp (P3c: the Map leaf's mark under `?`, its inside passing, S5.0g:P-R5); brackets br, braces iop (P3b); x, _, 0 and every record owp (P3c). Paths: S5.0g:R3 (a pairing refusal is replaced by the ancestor's class).

Subject on `? group G`: Some(x) ok (P3a); None atc (P5); brackets br, braces iop, map notation mna (P3b); x, _, 0, G { a: x, .. } and G { a: x, b: y, .. } owp (P3c: their inside passes against G); G { a: x } rmc (S5.0g:P-R5: the advice Some(G { a: x }) is refused again by L4, so the inside's refusal is named; a kind refusal, it stands under a path). Paths: S5.0g:R3 (a pairing refusal is replaced by the ancestor's class).

Subject on a List collection of G: brackets are its instance mark (P2): [x, ..], [x] and [x, r @ ..] ok (P3a; Q2: an ordered collection's value item is its front instance; P6 at the instances' root), [..] ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint), [.., x] ok by the principles (P2: the back instance, Q2: as a value), the product's ils being the stated limitation of a List collection's back instance kept in place, here read with the result leaving the cell out (a [cell-exception]; the product creates or removes instances at the back, and reads and updates them at the front); braces ils (P3b: the instance mark of the other order); Some/None pop, map notation mna (P3b); x, _, 0, G { a: x, .. } and G { a: x, b: y, .. } cwi (P3c: a value where the collection has its instances, its inside passing against G); G { a: x } rmc (S5.0g:P-R5: L4 refuses the instance record the advice writes). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a Set or Map collection of G, the result leaving or writing it alike: every bracket spelling ils (S5.0g:P-R4: brackets are a List collection's instance mark, of the wrong order here, whatever they hold); { G { a: x, .. }, .. } ok (P3a: an instance record in braces, the collection's rest framed, P6; it binds, so no lint, Q1); Some/None pop, map notation mna (P3b); x, _, 0, G { a: x, .. } and G { a: x, b: y, .. } cwi (P3c, their inside passing against G); G { a: x } rmc (S5.0g:P-R5). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on the computation, the result writing it: [..] ok without the lint (Q1's lint is for a cell the result leaves out). Some/None pop, braces iop, map mna (P3b); [x, ..] and [x] ok (P3a); [.., x] cbi (E1, S5.0g:F-6: inside the mark, standing under a path); [x, r @ ..] cir (Q3, inside the mark, standing under a path); x, _, 0 and the records cw (P3c, E2). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a plain Int or Set leaf, the result writing it: _ ok without the lint (Q1). Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop (design:R4 on the Set leaf), map mna (P3b); x ok; 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a List leaf, the result writing it: [..] and _ ok without the lint (Q1). Every bracket spelling ok (P3a, P6; the builtin List is matched at either end); braces iop, map mna, Some/None pop (P3b); x ok; 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a cons leaf, the result writing it: [.., x] cons-list-back-item (S5.0g:P-R1, P0: a cons list's back lowers to no K; inside the leaf's mark, it stands under a path); [..] and _ ok without the lint (Q1); [x, ..], [x] and [x, r @ ..] ok (P3a, P6); braces iop, map mna, Some/None pop (P3b); x ok; 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a Map leaf, the result writing it: _ ok without the lint (Q1). { y -> x, .. } ok (P3a); brackets br, braces iop, Some/None pop (P3b); x ok; 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on the group G, the result writing it: _ ok without the lint (Q1). Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x ok; 0 sort; G { a: x, .. } and G { a: x, b: y, .. } ok (P6); G { a: x } rmc (L4, a kind refusal). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on `? leaf Int`, the result writing it: None ok (P5: the result creates the cell, so K can test its absence); Some(x) ok (P3a); brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); values and records owp (P3c, the inside passing, S5.0g:P-R5). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on `? leaf List`, the result writing it: None ok (P5); Some(x) ok (P3a); every bracket spelling owp (P3c: the List leaf's mark under `?`, S5.0g:R7); braces iop, map mna (P3b); values and records owp (P3c). Paths: S5.0g:R3.
Subject on `? leaf Map`, the result writing it: None ok (P5); Some(x) ok (P3a); { y -> x, .. } owp (P3c); brackets br, braces iop (P3b); values and records owp (P3c). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on `? group G`, the result writing it: None ok (P5); Some(x) ok (P3a); brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, _, 0 and the open and vacuous records owp (P3c, their inside passing against G); G { a: x } rmc (S5.0g:P-R5: L4 refuses the advice Some(G { a: x }) again). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Subject on a List collection of G, the result writing it: [..] ok without the lint (Q1). [x, ..], [x] and [x, r @ ..] ok (P3a, Q2), [.., x] ok (P2: the back instance, Q2: as a value, which the result's [..] removes, P6); braces ils, Some/None pop, map mna (P3b); values and the open and vacuous records cwi (P3c); G { a: x } rmc (S5.0g:P-R5). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Result over the computation matched by `[y, ..]`: [x, ..] sort (P6: `..` keeps the subject's rest; x to the lattice); [x] rm (it drops the subject's `..`, P6); [..] ok (it keeps the rest and drops y); [.., x] cbi (E1, S5.0g:F-6: a kind refusal inside the mark, before pairing); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern (S5.0:F2) and _ wop (P4 placement, before the kind); Some/None pop, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } cw (P3c, E2; the vacuous `..` leaves nothing open, S5.0g:R4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (S5.0g:R4: a built record leaving b open, named before the missing wrapper since the advice puts it at a term's position, S5.0g:P-R5). Paths: S5.0g:R3 (a pairing refusal is replaced by the ancestor's class). The alias, wop, cbi and the open record are form or kind answers and stand.

Result over a plain Int or Set leaf, matched by the binder `old` or not matched (Q1's overwrite), alike since no rest is paired: Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern (S5.0:F2) and _ wop (P4 placement, before the kind); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } sort (P5: the new content, its sort to the lattice; the vacuous `..`, S5.0g:R4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (S5.0g:R4: a built term's record leaving b open, where Rust reads defaults and K keeps, P0; a kind answer, it stands). Paths: S5.0g:R3.

Result over a List leaf matched by `[y, ..]` (P6 at its content root): [x, ..] and [.., x] sort (they keep the rest; the builtin List has both ends), [..] ok, [x] rm (it drops the subject's `..`); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } rm (a whole value drops the subject's `..`); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern (S5.0:F2) and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (S5.0g:R4, at the kind step, before pairing); Some/None pop, braces iop, map mna (P3b). rm in every form (P6 at each content root, S5.0g:D-1: a group or instance record's children are entries of their own cells): a child's result drops its other side's rest, or writes a `..` its other side never wrote. The other side is the subject record's same child, an unmatched child where the subject does not name it (Q1's overwrite), the labelled subject instance's same child in an update `..me` (design:rev4-R10), and none to keep for a created instance's child, a `?` cell created over `None` (P5), or an update of a value matched elsewhere, which creates its instance (S5.0g:P-R3: `me` is bound).

column5: W { g: G { a: x, b: y }, n: 0 }

column3: sort in every form (P1, P6): each child's rest pairs with its own other side, and each value to the lattice. An exact child over a framed one or none; a created instance's exact child or bare `..` (template fields, P6); an update `..me` of a shown instance keeping or naming its key as the subject's binder or literal (S5.0g:D-2, S5.0g:R9); a vacuous `..` (S5.0g:R4); a `?` cell created over `None` taking its template's fields for a bare `..` (S5.0g:P-R13).

map-collection-key in every form: a Map collection's instance keeps its key, its first child (S5.0g:D-2): an update of a shown instance writing it as anything but its subject's key binder or the same literal (S5.0g:R9), or a key the labelled instance does not name, is a key change (P0); a created instance must write it (S5.0g:key).

An overwritten group's computation child (S5.0g:D-1, Q1): readable and claim cir (Q3: a readable rule never drops the continuation it did not match); cells! sort (the exact new computation; cells! may drop it, P7).
uor in every form: an overwritten group's `?` child, written Some(..) or None, has a presence the rule does not know (Q1 with P5).
open-record-outside-pattern in every form: an overwritten group's group child exists, so its bare `..` is Rust's defaults, which only a created instance has (S5.0:F3, S5.0g:D-1).

An update whose label the subject does not show, of a record of its constructor matched elsewhere (S5.0g:P-R3): readable and claim sort (a created instance taking that record's fields, P6); cells! record-remainder-in-cells-term (the reference notation names every child, and its one update rewrites in place the instance its subject labels, design:rev4-R10; ruled 2026-11-06, S6-1d-2), after its children pair against the instance it would create.
record-missing-children in every form: a `?` cell created over `None` is written by its record, which names every child or writes `..` (L4, S5.0g:D-4), whatever its creation.

record-update-base in every form (S5.0g:P-R3, P0): an update `..me` whose label names no instance the subject matches, with nothing else in the sentence binding `me`, has no base: it is no in-place rewrite, since K rewrites in place only an instance the left side matched, and no value builds a new instance.

Subject group records naming a Map, List or computation child, framed or exact: readable and claim ok (P5: they constrain and bind; a fresh readable binder takes its position's sort), cells! sort (a cells! binder is typed, the lattice's). The field's value is its child's entry and content root (P1, P6, S5.0g:F-1), so its `..` matches the child's rest in both forms (P7).

Result writing a group's Map child with a rest over the subject's child with one: sort in every form (P6 at the child's content root: `..` keeps the rest the subject's child framed; S5.0g:F-1: the fragment field's k::map![.., ..] is that root, as readable's { y -> x, .. } is, P7); the product's arm is design:M3's stated limitation; the product's readable and claim `mrr` is the same design:M3 limitation for a map read with a rest at a group record's child, a [cell-exception] (S5.0g item 3a fixes, F-8).

Result writing a group's Map child with a rest over a subject child that is exact or not named: rm in every form (P6: a result `..` the subject's child did not match, the unnamed child being unmatched, S5.0g:D-1; S5.0g:F-1 makes the cells! fragment field the child's content root, P7); the product's arm is design:M3's limitation, met at its form step first; the product's readable and claim `mrr` is the same design:M3 limitation for a map read with a rest at a group record's child, a [cell-exception] (S5.0g item 3a fixes, F-8).

Result writing a group's Map, List or computation child whose rest is not the subject child's: rm in every form (P6 at the child's content root, S5.0g:D-1, S5.0g:F-1: an exact child drops the `..` the subject's child framed, and a `..` keeps none where the subject's child is exact or not named); no map literal keeps a rest, so no design:M3 limitation shows.

Result writing a group's Map, List or computation child with the subject child's rest, both with one or both exact: sort in every form (P6 at the child's content root, S5.0g:D-1, S5.0g:F-1: `..` keeps the subject's rest, an exact child writes the whole content; the values to the lattice).

Result writing a group's computation child with a rest where the subject does not name the child: readable and claim cir (Q3: a readable rule neither keeps nor drops unmatched the continuation, a pairing answer), cells! rm (P6: a `..` the subject's child never matched, S5.0g:F-1). Both refuse, as P7 asks of admission.
